name: Cava
terms: Denominación de Origen Calificada, a step above DO for regions with a record of consistent quality. Only Rioja and Priorat hold it.
Denominación de Origen, Spain's main quality tier.
Spain's regional wine tier, below DO.
A single-estate wine of high quality. A pago is a vineyard estate.
Young wine, sold with little or no aging. Some see a few months in oak.
Spanish sparkling wine made by the traditional method, mostly from Macabeo, Parellada and Xarel·lo. Other methods cannot use the name.
keyfacts: Only wines made by the traditional method may be labeled cava.
More than 95% of cava is produced in the Comtats de Barcelona zone of Catalonia, whose heart is Sant Sadurní d'Anoia in Penedès.
Macabeo, Parellada and Xarel·lo are the most traditional cava grapes, and Chardonnay and Malvasia are also permitted.
Authorized red grapes are Garnacha tinta, Monastrell, Trepat and Pinot Noir, and rosé cava base wines must contain at least 25% red grapes.
The term cava was officially approved for Spanish sparkling wine in 1972, when the Regulatory Council of Sparkling Wines was set up.

notes: Cava is a sparkling wine that ferments and ages in bottle, named for the cellars where this happens.
Macabeo and Xarel·lo are key grapes, and some top Cavas are led by Xarel·lo.

blurb.text: A Spanish DO for quality sparkling wine, made only by the traditional method as in Champagne. Macabeo, Parellada and Xarello are the traditional grapes. Other allowed grapes include Chardonnay and the reds Pinot Noir, Garnacha Tinta, Monastrell and Trepat. About 95 percent of cava comes from the Penedès area.
